content:
Since the Lean VS Code extension provides such an insanely good UX, I've found myself noticing a paper cut which I'm wondering if it's a simple oversight:

When hovering over terms in the info view, there's a popup which shows the type of the term. Those terms in the popup are then again fully interactive and can, e.g., be Cmd/Ctrl-clicked to go to the definition.
In contrast, when hovering over terms in the source code, the popup does not produce interactive terms, and, e.g., Cmd/Ctrl-clicked does not work:

Hover in info view vs source code

Is it possible to have the same interactive behaviour for the source code hover, or is there some limitation preventing this?
AFAIK VSCode only lets you supply markdown for hovers, whereas the infoview is HTML

We fully control the InfoView, but editor hovers are fully controlled by VS Code and limited to either Markdown or a "safe" HTML subset. For the "safe" HTML subset, editor hovers also don't interact particularly well with dynamic content, e.g. #general > Showing two doc-string @ 💬.

So I don't think interactive hovers are in scope for editor hovers, but we could in principle provide go-to-definition by turning some identifiers into local file links.
There are some open questions related to this idea though, e.g. whether we can still get the hover code block syntax highlighting to work while also turning some identifiers into links and which identifiers we want to turn into links in the first place so that not every single piece of text in the popup turns blue.

This topic has been in my backlog for a while ... :-)

(These are interactive in the hover as well already in lean.nvim without much effort on our part :)

Though me interactivity to hovers of declaration bodies too has caused some bugs which I need to fix.
